Subject: Operational demarcation & egress proofing — initial ask

Avery / Redwood team,

Thanks for the quick intro last week. We're kicking off the operational handoff for our private VPC deployment (Orion pilot) and need a concise reference for the demarcation and egress constraints so our infra/security teams can start the allowlist and audit planning. High level asks: 

- Control plane endpoints (FQDNs / IPs) we should allow from our tenant subnets
- Outbound egress behavior: do control plane calls originate from customer subnet IPs or from Redwood-managed NATs?
- Recommended minimal egress CIDRs (for telemetry, telemetry ingestion, artifact fetch) and whether CIDRs are stable or region-specific
- TLS/mTLS expectations for the data/control plane and how cert rotation is handled
- KMS/HSM options and whether keys are customer-managed (bring-your-own) or Redwood-managed
- Evidence we can include in our compliance workbook (SOC2 artifact names / audit log examples / runbook link)

Attached is our current reference diagram (orion_vpc_reference_diagram_v3.pdf) showing where we'd like the demarcation to sit. For scheduling, we can do a 30m call next Tue or Wed — timezone PST.

Appreciate a short bulletized runbook we can pass along to NetOps.

Thanks,
Danielle
Danielle Park

Orion Networks

Attachments we will send: egress-ip-proposal.csv (proposed Redwood NAT / egress IP ranges), and a mutual TLS matrix that shows where client certs are required. We will also include an evidence checklist mapping Redwood audit artifacts to SOC2 categories.

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>

Subject: Technical details — control plane FQDNs, egress CIDRs, and TLS

Danielle — great call earlier. As promised, here are the concrete details you can use in your allowlist and evidence workbook. I'll put this into the runbook doc after your confirmation.

1) Control plane endpoints (DNS names — allow outbound HTTPS to these FQDNs from tenant subnets):
   - control-api.us.redwood-inference.com
   - uploads.us.redwood-inference.com
   - metrics-collector.us.redwood-inference.com
   (We use regional DNS with global-anycast; IPs are not guaranteed stable for customer NAT mode)

2) Redwood-managed egress (recommended if you need a fixed IP set for onboarding):
   - We can provide a static pool per account. Current proposal (attached egress-ip-proposal.csv) lists 6 x IPv4 /32s in the US region.
   - Change policy: we provide 90-day notice for planned changes; emergency rotations will be communicated via your escalation channel.

3) Customer-managed NAT mode (recommended for regulated tenants):
   - Outbound calls originate from your NAT IPs; keep outbound HTTPS (443) to the control FQDNs and outbound to S3-compatible artifact endpoints (443).
   - Ports: 443 only for control/data plane. For KV cache streaming we use websocket-over-https; no additional ports required.

4) TLS and mTLS:
   - Control plane: TLS 1.2+ TLS with server certs; mutual TLS (client certs) is optional but recommended for stricter isolation.
   - For BYOK with HSM: we support Google Cloud KMS, AWS KMS with external key store, and customer HSM via PKCS#11 for on-prem HSM appliances. Key wrapping is supported for AES-256 keys.
   - Cert rotation: we support automatic server cert rotation; for client certs we recommend short-lived certs (30d) with ACME or a similar provisioning flow. We'll share a mutual_tls_matrix.xlsx showing required flows and tooling suggestions.

5) Audit artifacts (SOC2 / evidence):
   - Audit logs: request-id mapped request traces for each control-plane call (retain 90 days standard, extended retention available as add-on).
   - Runbook artifact: "private-vpc-allowlist-and-egress-proof-v1.0" (we'll upload to the Drive link provided).
   - Evidence samples: a sample signed TLS cert rotation event, a sample request trace for a tenant-initiated model load, and a service account key rotation log.

6) Operational notes:
   - For cutover we recommend a staged allowlist test: 1) Redwood-managed egress to allowlist verify; 2) customer NAT cutover in low-traffic window; 3) telemetry validation and golden traffic replay.

Attaching: egress-ip-proposal.csv, mutual_tls_matrix.xlsx.

Let us know if you want the egress pool represented as CIDR aggregates instead of /32s.

—Soojin
